flows.title: Make a photo avatar
steps: Go to the Avatars tab and choose New Avatar, then Upload Photo — or Design with AI to generate one instead.
Upload the photo, give the avatar a name, and submit it for creation.
Wait for the avatar look to be validated. Once that finishes it can be used across the platform.
A photo works best when the face is close to human proportions, with eyes, mouth and lips clearly visible and the character large in the frame.

flows.title: Put a photo avatar into a video
steps: Go to the Avatars tab and select your avatar.
Click the arrow icon on the avatar to take it straight into Studio. The heart button marks it a favourite so it appears first wherever an avatar is chosen.
In Studio, choose a Voice for the avatar.
Still in Studio, open the Avatar tab and click the small arrow under Motion Engine to pick from the engines available to you.
Advanced Settings adds a custom motion prompt when a scene needs particular gestures or body language.

flows.title: Work through an explainer video
steps: Decide what the video is for, then draft a short script — the guide suggests 60 to 90 seconds, opening with a hook, then the problem, the solution, how it works, the benefits and a closing call to action.
Choose a public avatar from the library, or make a custom one, and match it with a voice.
Design the scenes: browse HeyGen's templates or build your own, and upload assets such as product images, videos, animations, music or screen recordings.
Refine it in HeyGen's text-based editor, which keeps scenes, text and transitions lined up with the script.
Click Generate, then download or share the finished video. Captions help on platforms that autoplay silently.
